headline: Negeri Sembilan Throne: Three of the Four Undang Titles Are Now Contested
context: On 19 April 2026, four signatories, each claiming an Undang title, issued a proclamation purporting to depose Tuanku Muhriz and chose Tunku Nadzaruddin to succeed him. Tuanku Muhriz continues to carry out the Ruler's functions.

cards.text: On 15 September the state exco backed a 19 April proclamation to depose Tuanku Muhriz. Two days later the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) called it invalid.
cards.sub: The DKU, the state's council on custom, says three of the four signatories were not lawful Undangs at the time. They say they were.

cards.h: Article X lets Undangs call on a Ruler to abdicate after a 'full and complete enquiry'. Article XXIX counts their powers as duly used when at least three act.
cards.s: The DKU says no full enquiry was held; the AGC found no facts showing Article X was followed. The four say they held one on 5 March.

cards.h: Mubarak Thahak, who read the 19 April proclamation, proclaimed Tuanku Muhriz Ruler as Undang of Sungai Ujong in 2008.
cards.s: On 5 June his side proclaimed Tunku Nadzaruddin. The DKU calls it contempt of a same-day order; the six it named say only a Special Court can hear it. A stay bid failed on 4 November.

cards.h: The DKU says Sungai Ujong's elders removed Mubarak in May 2025, Jelebu's removed Maarof Mat Rashad in May 2023, and Abdul Rahim Yasin was never installed in Rembau.
cards.s: Article XVI(3) makes such advice final and non-justiciable. The four reject it and say they remain the Undangs.

cards.h: Article X's proclamation also needs the Menteri Besar's signature. MB Ismail Lasim signed on 3 August and later cited duress; a lawyer for the six says he signed freely.
cards.s: On 20 September Tuanku Muhriz revoked 10 exco appointments. Ismail objected; the Attorney-General called the revocation valid.

cards.text: This was a dispute over Undangs before it became one over a Ruler. The throne now depends on who lawfully held three Undang titles on 19 April.
No side disputes that Undangs may remove a Ruler. Whether they lawfully did on 19 April is a question every side has answered and no court has.
